post.description:
Synchronous (default): responds once the LLM has written the questions and they passed the schema and rule checks (with up to one repair call). If generation fails, the quiz is kept with status "failed" and a failureReason, and the error response includes its `quizId`.

With `stream: true`: creates the quiz as "generating", returns 202 `{ quizId }` at once, and generates in the background; watch it at GET /api/quizzes/{quizId}/stream. Generation errors then arrive as a `problem` event on that stream.

Multiple-choice options are shuffled before saving.

get.description:
A text/event-stream. First every saved question is replayed, so a reconnecting client catches up; then the live events while generation runs. Events:
- `question`: a validated, saved question (QuestionResponse)
- `question_rejected`: `{ position, violations }` for a line that failed validation; the repair step fills its position later
- `done`: `{ generated, rejected, usage }`; the stream ends
- `problem`: problem details (generation failed, or unknown quiz); the stream ends

Disconnecting does not stop generation. Works for synchronously generated quizzes too (replay, then `done`).

From a terminal: `curl -N http://localhost:3000/api/quizzes/{id}/stream`

info.title: QuizForge API
info.description:
Turns a lesson into a reviewed quiz: an LLM drafts the questions, a teacher edits, approves, rejects or regenerates them, then publishes the quiz.

Every error is an RFC 9457 problem details response (`application/problem+json`).

type.description: A URI identifying the problem type. "about:blank" means the HTTP status says it all.

title.description: Short summary of the problem type.

detail.description: What went wrong this time. Never contains prompts, lesson text or model output.
detail.example: A published quiz and its questions can no longer be changed.

instance.description: The request path that produced the problem.

pointer.description: JSON Pointer to the offending request body field, e.g. "#/options/3".

parameter.description: Name of the offending query or path parameter, e.g. "limit" or "id".

detail.description: What is wrong. When neither pointer nor parameter is set, it is about the request as a whole.

content.description: The lesson text, 200 to 20000 characters after trimming (400 if shorter, 413 if longer). Treated as data, never as instructions to the model.
content.example: A recursive function is a function that calls itself to solve a smaller version of the same problem. Every recursive function needs a base case, which is a condition where the function returns a result without calling itself. Without a base case, the function would call itself forever.

quizCounts.description: The lesson's quizzes, counted by status (zeros included).

total.description: All lessons, not just this page.

difficulty.description: easy: recall of stated facts; medium: understanding or applying an idea; hard: combining several parts of the lesson.

types.description: Question types the quiz may use.

stream.description: true: return 202 { quizId } at once and stream the questions from GET /api/quizzes/{quizId}/stream. Absent or false: generate synchronously and return the quiz (201).

stem.example: What is the base case of a recursive function?

options.description: Multiple choice: 4 options, shuffled when the question was generated. True/false: ["True", "False"].
example: The first call made to the function
A condition where the function returns a result without calling itself
The deepest call on the call stack
A loop that replaces the recursion

explanation.example: The lesson defines the base case as the condition where the function returns without calling itself.

sourceQuote.description: The sentence of the lesson that supports the answer.
sourceQuote.example: a base case, which is a condition where the function returns a result without calling itself

editedAt.description: When a teacher last changed the content; null if never.

isEdited.description: Whether the content now differs from the AI's version: stem, explanation, the set of options or the correct answer. Reordering options, or changing only case or whitespace, does not count. The edit rate uses the same rule.

failureReason.description: Why the quiz failed; null unless status is "failed".

questions.description: Current questions in order. Once published, only the approved ones.

position.description: The position the rejected line would have had.

violations.description: Why the line was rejected. Never quotes the model output.
example: question 3: sourceQuote does not appear in the lesson

costUsd.description: USD as a decimal string with 6 places.

generated.description: Questions saved, including those filled in by the repair step.

rejected.description: Lines the model wrote that failed validation.

usage.description: Every LLM call made for the quiz so far.

failureReason.description: Why the quiz failed; null unless status is "failed".

questionCount.description: How many questions the quiz has: approved ones once published, otherwise all current ones (replaced questions never count). Compare with settings.count.

editRate.description: Approved questions whose content differs from the model original, divided by approved questions. Reordering options is not an edit. Null with no approved questions.

rejectRate.description: rejected / (approved + rejected); drafts are undecided. Null when nothing is decided.

missRate.description: (rejected + regenerated) / (approved + rejected + regenerated): how often the model question was not good enough.

calls.description: LLM calls (one per generation or regeneration request).

attempts.description: Provider requests, retries and repair calls included.

costUsd.description: USD as a decimal string with 6 places, never a float.

stem.example: What makes a recursive function stop?

options.description: Multiple choice: exactly 4 distinct options, no "all/none of the above". True/false: must stay ["True", "False"].

explanation.example: The function stops calling itself once it reaches the base case.

status.description: draft -> approved or rejected; approved or rejected -> draft. Anything else is a 409; the current status is a no-op.
